proposal: The Mandate recommends that the NRC finish light-water reactor combined license and design certification reviews generally within two years and early site permits within one year, speed license extensions with a streamlined NEPA review, replace the ALARA principle with clear risk-based dose standards, and work with Congress to limit licensee fees to entity-specific activities.

Codify the 12 and 18 month decision deadlines in rule; the FY2026 fee rule says this will come in a future rulemaking. The Mandate's own targets are two years for combined licenses and design certifications and one year for early site permits.

Fee recommendation: the Mandate asks Congress to limit licensee fees to entity-specific activities with other costs appropriated; the FY2026 fee rule targets fee recovery of the budget net of statutory exclusions (ADVANCE Act exclusions amount to 40.0 million dollars) and no statute changing the fee approach was found.

status_summary: Executive Order 14300 (signed 2025-05-23) directs the NRC to set maximum decision periods of 18 months for new reactor applications and 1 year for continued operation, reconsider ALARA and the linear no-threshold model, and issue final rules within 18 months. The NRC has finalized several streamlining rules, including a 40-year design certification duration (effective 2025-09-15), the advanced reactor framework and categorical exclusions (2026-03-30), generic environmental findings for new reactors (2026-04-24) and FY2026 fees with fixed service-fee caps (2026-06-16), and has published three direct final rules not yet in effect as of 2026-10-18: NRC rulemaking procedure modernization (published 2026-08-11, effective date of 2026-10-26 confirmed on 2026-09-30), materials licensing exemptions (published 2026-10-05, effective 2026-12-21 absent significant adverse comment) and a 40-year AP1000 design certification renewal (published 2026-10-14, effective 2026-12-28 absent significant adverse comment). The ALARA replacement (2026-07-15), the NEPA implementation proposal (2026-07-07), the reactor licensing and siting proposal (2026-07-16) and the licensing, decommissioning and oversight proposal (2026-09-24) are proposed rules only, and the FY2026 fee rule states the 12 and 18 month decision deadlines will be addressed in a future rulemaking. The Mandate's fee recommendation to Congress has no enacted counterpart found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14300 (signed 2025-05-23, published in the Federal Register 2025-05-29, document 2025-09798) directs the NRC in section 5 to set maximum decision periods of 18 months for new reactor applications and 1 year for continued operation, enforced through caps on hourly fee recovery, to reconsider the linear no-threshold model and ALARA, and to issue proposed rules within 9 months and final rules within 18 months.
NRC confirms the 2025-09-15 effective date of its direct final rule (published 2025-07-02) extending design certification duration from 15 to 40 years.
NRC publishes a final rule adding a risk-informed, technology-inclusive licensing framework for commercial nuclear plants, including advanced reactors that do not use light-water technology.

NRC publishes a final rule on categorical exclusions from environmental review (effective 2026-04-29); the NRC says the rulemaking was under way before Executive Order 14300 and that expanding exclusions for new reactor licensing was outside the rule's scope.

NRC publishes a final rule (91 FR 22394, effective 2026-05-26) codifying generic environmental findings for licensing new nuclear reactors; the NRC describes this rulemaking as separate from its Executive Order 14300 reform.

NRC publishes its FY2026 fee rule (effective 2026-08-17) with fixed caps on service fees under Executive Order 14300 section 5(a), effective 2026-10-01, and states the 12 and 18 month decision deadlines will be addressed in a future rulemaking; about 818.8 million of 971.5 million dollars in budget authority is targeted for fee recovery.

NRC publishes a proposed rule (91 FR 42086) on implementing the National Environmental Policy Act that would limit NEPA reviews to effects within NRC's statutory authority, revise review-level procedures and add categorical exclusions; comments due 2026-08-21.

NRC publishes the radiation protection proposed rule (91 FR 43456): it would remove the term ALARA from the regulations in favor of a graded approach to dose management (pp. 43456, 43465, 43468), keep current dose limits (p. 43464) and reaffirm the linear dose-response model while not applying its nonthreshold aspect in the ALARA context (pp. 43462 to 43464). Comments due 2026-08-31.

NRC publishes a proposed rule (91 FR 44560) to modernize reactor licensing, safety oversight and siting under 10 CFR Parts 2, 50, 51, 52, 53, 54, 71 and 100, citing Executive Order 14300; comments due 2026-08-31.

NRC publishes a direct final rule (91 FR 51555), NRC Modernization: Rulemaking Procedure, FACA Alignment, Access, and Security, stated to respond to Executive Order 14300; effective 2026-10-26 unless significant adverse comments are received by 2026-09-10, with a companion proposed rule.

NRC publishes a proposed rule (91 FR 60702), Regulatory Enhancements for Reactor Licensing, Decommissioning, and Operational Oversight, stated to respond to section 5 of Executive Order 14300; comments due 2026-11-09.

NRC publishes a correction and confirmation of effective date (91 FR 61685) confirming that its 2026-08-11 direct final rule on rulemaking procedure, Federal Advisory Committee Act alignment, access and security takes effect 2026-10-26.

NRC publishes a direct final rule, Exemptions From Materials Licensing (91 FR 63133), described as deregulatory and citing Executive Order 14300; effective 2026-12-21 unless significant adverse comments arrive by 2026-11-04, with a companion proposed rule the same day.

NRC publishes a direct final rule (91 FR 65091) renewing the AP1000 design certification for 40 years from its effective date and adopting Revision 20 of the design control document; effective 2026-12-28 unless significant adverse comments arrive by 2026-11-13, with a companion proposed rule.

The Federal Register abstract of the ALARA proposal does not use the term; the full text does (pp. 43456, 43468). The 2026-05-20 POWER Magazine report (5 of 27 planned rulemakings final; the chair conceding some final rules would follow the order's target of about 2026-11-23) is a news report and is not counted as an event; it was not re-opened. The ANS report of 2026-03-13 said the NRC was on target for the deadline; the later report is used. The NRC confirmed on 2026-09-30 the 2026-10-26 effective date of the 2026-08-11 direct final rule; the comment periods on the 2026-10-05 and 2026-10-14 direct final rules were still open on 2026-10-18, and none of the three had taken effect by then. A Federal Register API listing of NRC rules from 2026-08-01 showed no final ALARA, reactor licensing or NEPA implementation rule. The Federal Register abstract of the generic environmental findings rule describes it as separate from the Executive Order 14300 reform. The NRC's own count of final rules after May 2026 was not found. Whether any licensing review has met the 18 month limit was not checked. Staffing reductions, ACRS changes and commissioner changes were not researched. Context from the DOE side, not NRC licensing: CRS R48599 (updated 2026-03-25) lists the Office of Nuclear Energy at 1,685.0 million dollars enacted for FY2026 against a 1,370.0 million request; the enacting law is believed to be Public Law 119-74, Division B, but its text on govinfo was truncated and the amount was not confirmed there. POWER Magazine's report on the DOE Nuclear Energy Launch Pad ties it to Executive Order 14301, so it is not counted toward this record. ADVANCE Act implementation and the Part 53 details beyond the 2026-03-30 framework rule were not examined.
